title: Health Care Workers Are Tired of Cleaning Up Palantir’s Mess
gist: Nurses across HCA Healthcare say the Palantir-built Timpani AI scheduling tool, deployed at about 130 of 190 hospitals, under-staffs shifts and ignores preferences, prompting union grievances and a whistleblower suit, while HCA claims efficiency gains. Similar Foundry-based problems at Rayus Radiology and NHS backlash show reputational risk even as Palantir sales near $2B per quarter.

insights.claim: HCA, the largest US hospital chain, has deployed Timpani, an AI nurse-scheduling tool co-developed with Palantir, at roughly 130 of its 190 locations since 2023.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Shows scale of Palantir's healthcare deployment and exposure to HCA labor risk.

insights.claim: Timpani is built on Palantir Foundry and uses algorithmic forecasts of patient volumes and staffing needs to automatically build nursing schedules.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Foundry is the reusable platform behind multiple healthcare products, so failures can propagate across customers.
insights.locator: Timpani was built on Palantir Foundry

insights.claim: HCA executive Michael Schlosser claims Timpani cut manager scheduling hours, lowered reliance on costly contract nurses, and increased retention, with over 98 percent of schedules including a mix of skill and experience.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Management ROI claims are unaudited and contested by nurses; watch for independent verification.
insights.quote: The efficiency comes from AI generating stronger initial schedules
insights.locator: Schlosser said in a paper this past July

insights.claim: HCA says Timpani schedules nurses on only 1 percent of requested days off, though a Missouri nurse says any such assignment was previously unheard of at their facility.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: A low headline error rate can mask large perceived service degradation among workers.

insights.claim: Nurses at multiple HCA sites allege Timpani routinely under-staffs shifts, lacks experienced veterans especially on Sundays, and ignores stated shift preferences, with minimal oversight.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Alleged staffing imbalance is a patient-safety and liability risk for HCA.
insights.locator: The nurses who spoke with WIRED allege

insights.claim: Nurses say Timpani increased time spent on shift trades and appeals versus manual scheduling, and that call-outs are rising, though excess absences risk termination.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Scheduling friction can drive attrition and absenteeism, offsetting claimed retention gains.

insights.claim: Appeals now go to a centralized HCA headquarters team in Nashville with no direct communication, and nurses estimate shift-swap success after denial at only about 50 percent.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Centralization removed local manager discretion, a design choice behind the human-oversight complaints.
insights.locator: At HCA, some nurses also want Palantir gone

insights.claim: A Missouri HCA psychiatric-center nurse leader claims several colleagues quit over Timpani and workplace injuries rose in the first 12 months with the tool.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Single-site, unverified claim, but a signal of possible turnover and injury costs.
insights.locator: Barker, who is a National Nurses United leader

insights.claim: National Nurses United, representing about 10,000 of HCA's 100,000 nurses, says HCA rejected its information requests about Timpani, and a roughly 500-nurse unit filed a grievance likely headed to arbitration.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: AI scheduling is becoming a collective-bargaining flashpoint; watch arbitration outcomes.

insights.claim: A former HCA data science manager, Angelique Russell, sued in July alleging retaliatory firing after raising Timpani concerns and claiming HCA routinely deleted data the tool uses, preventing audits and possibly violating healthcare laws.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Whistleblower litigation could force discovery of Timpani performance data; HCA has yet to respond in court.
insights.locator: Some purported details emerged in July

insights.claim: Palantir's sales have nearly doubled to almost $2 billion per quarter as organizations seek help analyzing data and automating tasks, with cost and staffing pressures making health care providers eager customers.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Healthcare is a demand driver for Palantir's commercial growth.

insights.claim: Rayus Radiology reported errors from a Palantir Foundry-based scheduling tool, including linking orders to wrong patient profiles, mismatched scans, and invented patient details.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Similar failures across customers suggest platform-level quality and oversight risk as Palantir pushes into clinical workflows.
insights.locator: Rayus Radiology, a large US imaging chain

insights.claim: Palantir's UK NHS contract of $440 million, aimed at cutting appointment wait times, faces demands from nurses and activists to cancel it over privacy and security concerns.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Political and labor backlash is a contract-renewal and reputational risk for Palantir in public healthcare.

insights.claim: Cleveland Clinic credits Palantir software with boosting patient capacity by forecasting ER discharges and replacing manual coordination.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Positive reference customers show the product can work, so outcomes depend on implementation and oversight.

insights.claim: Palantir describes its software as merely presenting information more helpfully and says customers are responsible for data, policies and decisionmaking, a liability-shifting stance.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Palantir positions itself away from liability, pushing risk onto customers like HCA.
insights.locator: A Palantir spokesperson declined to comment
